text: Our galaxy's black hole eats an Earth's worth of gas... about every ten years.
Do you know who's feeding the monster in the middle of the Milky Way?
It's called Sagittarius A star. Four million times heavier than the Sun.
For years, astronomers watched strange glowing gas clouds diving toward it. Nobody knew where they came from.
Now they found the culprit. Two giant stars, so close they're touching.
Their winds blast out at thousands of kilometers per second... and smash into each other.
That crash squeezes gas into clumps... each about as heavy as Earth.
And then they fall. Straight toward the black hole.
Scientists say one clump every ten years is enough to keep it fed.
Bigger telescopes are coming, and astronomers expect to find more of these gas streams.
Which means we're about to watch a black hole's dinner... almost in real time.
Would you want to see it up close?
